observation.visible_scene: A perforated stainless-steel steamer insert holds several cooked, bright-red lobsters (claws banded with green and tan ties) and rests inside a larger dark pan against a grey, smudged metal wall. Wisps of steam hang above the tray. The lobsters are arranged with one large body in the centre, a tail section toward the lower right, and claw clusters at the left.
visible_changes: Steam continuously rises and drifts above the tray, its shape and density shifting from frame to frame while the lobsters themselves do not move relative to the tray.

The framing drifts slowly: the tray and its contents shift leftward within the image and the far rim of the tray moves higher in the frame, so that by the later frames a second, empty, bright metal pan becomes visible along the right edge.
Overall exposure/contrast changes modestly across the clip (mid-frames appear darker, the right-hand pan appears lighter as it enters view).
The relative positions of the lobsters to one another and to the tray walls stay constant throughout the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: The heat source or cooking process producing the steam is not shown.
Whether the lobsters were freshly steamed or are being held warm, and any action before or after this segment, is unknown.
The purpose of the adjacent empty pan is not visible.
uncertain_details: The exact camera motion (pan versus handheld drift versus slight tilt/zoom) cannot be separated cleanly; only the net leftward shift of the tray and the reveal of the right pan are clearly supported.
No lobster limb or body displacement is discernible beyond camera-induced framing changes.
